product.title: JSON Server
product.summary: Full fake REST API from a single JSON or JSON5 file, with filtering, sorting, pagination, and embedding, and writes saved back to the file.
problems: Mock a REST API for frontend prototyping without writing a backend
Serve a JSON file as a CRUD REST API
Fake backend for tests, demos, and tutorials
Try out an API shape before building the real server

workflows.title: Serve a JSON file as a REST API
workflows.description: Run json-server with a db.json or db.json5 file. Every top-level array becomes a collection with GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE routes (/posts, /posts/:id); every top-level object becomes a singular resource (/profile). The server assigns ids to new items and saves every change back to the file.

workflows.title: Filter, sort, paginate, and embed
workflows.description: Query collections with field operators (title:contains=foo, views:gt=100, and lt, lte, gte, eq, ne, in, startsWith, endsWith), a JSON _where filter, _sort (prefix - for descending), _page and _per_page pagination, and _embed to include related items. DELETE with _dependent removes related items too.

workflows.title: Serve static files next to the API
workflows.description: Files in ./public, and any directories passed with --static, are served alongside the API, so a prototype frontend and its mock backend run from one process. The home page lists the available resources.

limitations: Beta v1: usable but expect breaking changes; the stable line is v0.17
No authentication or authorization: anyone who can reach the port can read and change all data
The server listens on all network interfaces; --host and HOST only change the printed URLs
Data lives in one JSON file, held in memory and rewritten on every change; not suited to large datasets or concurrent writers
Query filters coerce numeric-looking values to numbers, so postId=1 does not match string ids such as "1"
Client-provided ids are ignored; the server generates random ids for new items
Built for prototyping, mocking, and tests, not production use

highlights.title: REST API with zero code
highlights.description: Every top-level array in the data file becomes a collection with GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE routes; objects become singular resources.

highlights.title: Filtering, sorting, pagination, embedding
highlights.description: Field operators (lt, gt, ne, in, contains, startsWith, ...), a JSON _where filter, _sort, _page and _per_page, and _embed for related items.

highlights.title: Changes persist to the file
highlights.description: Writes through the API are saved back to the JSON or JSON5 file, and edits made to the file by hand are reloaded live.

highlights.title: Static files and CORS
highlights.description: Serves ./public and extra --static directories next to the API, with CORS open to all origins for browser prototypes.

reuse.attribution: JSON Server is created by typicode and contributors (https://github.com/typicode/json-server). This release is published unchanged from the arielpollack/json-server fork.

configuration.name: PORT
configuration.description: Port the server listens on. Defaults to 3000; the --port flag overrides it.

configuration.name: HOST
configuration.description: Host shown in the printed endpoint URLs. Defaults to localhost; the --host flag overrides it. It does not restrict which interfaces the server listens on.

setup.title: Install dependencies and build
setup.description: Install the locked dependencies with pnpm and compile the TypeScript sources to lib/.

setup.title: Create your data file
setup.description: Start from fixtures/db.json (or db.json5) and replace the sample posts, comments, and profile with your own collections (top-level arrays) and singular resources (top-level objects). Then run node lib/bin.js db.json.

verify.description: With the server running, GET /<collection> for one of your collections returns 200 and your items

core.description: The node:test suite exercises the service layer (create, update, patch, delete with dependents, embedding), query parsing, pagination, and every REST route through the HTTP app against in-memory fixture data and a temporary file.

probes.description: Home page lists the resources in the data file
Filters posts with a field operator
Creates a post and returns it with a server-generated id
Rejects a body that is not a JSON object

bodyIncludes: Body must be a JSON object

probes.description: Unknown item id returns a JSON 404

storage: The JSON or JSON5 file passed on the command line, rewritten in place on every write
collected: None by the app itself; it stores whatever clients send to it in the data file

customizationPoints.description: Replace the sample posts, comments, and profile with your own resources
Home page template that lists the available resources
Static files served next to the API

replacedContent: Nothing was replaced: the source is upstream json-server 1.0.0-beta.15 unchanged, with saassy.json and .env.example added
assumptions: pnpm for development; the CI and npm publish workflows, funding link, and sponsor links in README are upstream typicode's
Sample fixture data uses typicode's handle as the profile name

costs.assumptions: Runs locally or on any Node.js host; that host's pricing applies
